A.test: A. cash tips increase cash only

B.test: B. digital earnings increase the selected digital account only

C.test: C. digital tips already included are not added twice; separate tips are added once

D.test: D. editing a day rewrites its legs: balances move by the difference, no duplicate income

E.test: E. a cash purchase reduces cash, not the bank

F.test: F. a debit purchase reduces the bank, not cash

G.test: G. a credit purchase raises what the card is owed; no cash leaves; Safe to Spend cash is unchanged

H.test: H. a card payment lowers the source and the card balance and is not new spending

I.test: I. a transfer between owned accounts creates no income and keeps total money the same

J.test: J. a cash deposit lowers cash and raises the bank

K.test: K. recurrence produces scheduled occurrences, never completed payments

L.test: L. marking a bill paid creates exactly one payment and moves to the next date

M.test: M. setting money aside moves no money and writes no ledger entry

N.test: N. $95 set aside toward a $140 bill is part of the $140 — Safe to Spend stays $360, not $265

O.test: O. the same money cannot silently fund two bills; later over-commitment is reported

P.test: P. utilization uses the card limit and balance; payment to a chosen target rounds up

Q.test: Q. payment guidance counts payments already made; a paid minimum leaves Safe to Spend

R.test: R. statement closing date and payment due date stay distinct

S.test: S. corrections and reversals keep history: deleted days and undone payments stay traceable

T.test: T. reloading from storage does not duplicate entries

U.test: U. two users never see each other’s records

V.test: V. manual and stale balances are never presented as bank-confirmed

W.test: W. missing card data produces an honest explanation, not a number

X.test: X. rounding and currency precision are consistent

Y.test: Y. month-end and leap-year schedules keep their day

Z.test: Z. one event is counted once across income, transfers, payments and the ledger

additional_invariants.test: one daily submission is one traceable event; the same source and day cannot be recorded twice
daily, weekly and monthly totals add each day once
earnings cannot be received into a credit card
transfers can be reversed as one event; money cannot move out of a credit card
a scheduled (future-dated) transfer changes nothing until its date
a balance correction after entries records the difference instead of re-counting
suggests the usual account by purpose, honours a chosen account, and explains when none fits
partial payments keep the occurrence open and cannot exceed what is due
paying a funded bill uses the set-aside money; extra is released or carried as chosen
reassigning set-aside money keeps it in the same account and respects the new cap
an account-specific shortfall is reported even when total Safe to Spend is positive
skip and reschedule change dates only; cancel keeps history and releases set-asides
subscription totals convert each frequency instead of adding them as monthly
interest guidance never promises interest avoidance when a balance is carried

data: synthetic accounts only (BANK 500, RIDESHARE payout card 240, CASH 100, VISA owes 400 of 2000)
